items.title: Bounded negative primitive-plan summary
source: beginMetalSubpass eligibility and incoming graphics state
items.current: Primary inline first subpass only, single subpass, no multiview/suspend/resume. Planner scans at most2048 commands; conversion entries256 and scratch64MiB. Ordinary draws are still possible shader writers. Incoming pipeline/render/index state may originate before the pass.
items.proposed: One pass-owned immutable summary can bypass the scan only when every command in the exact bounded interval proves no conversion for its actual initial state. Unknown selects the current planner. A first-draw or last-pipeline boolean is insufficient.
stateTable: Unknown; bind to precise pass interval and initial pipeline/dynamic/index signature
Preserve proof only for explicit recognized effects
Require exact pipeline, dynamic topology/restart/provoking/point state and no unproved shader effects
NoConversion only if every step proved; pool reset invalidates summary
counterexamples: First ordinary draw followed by a triangle fan or dynamic topology change
An ordinary shader-writing draw before a converted indexed draw
Same pass bytes replayed with a different inherited pipeline/index binding
2048-command truncation incorrectly treated as proof of a whole pass
Creating the summary by running the same lookahead twice merely moves/adds work
items.missing: No existing cheap, authoritative per-pass state summary or measured dominant negative scanning interval is identified. Adding a generic per-command summary currently expands recording work and ABI without demonstrated net benefit.
items.nextEvidence: Use an existing primitive-plan/recording trace to name a recurring negative interval and its initial state. Count existing scanned commands and useful conversions on that interval before choosing storage/hooks; no new broad collector suite.
verification: Compare exact plan entries and fallback boundaries with baseline for fan/restart/provoking/dynamic/zero draw and unknown command sequences
Require cancellation/pool-reuse invalidation, initial-state changes and cap exhaustion
Actual dependency handoff and index input lifetime fixture after implementation
items.activation: A cue resumes this detailed design and evidence selection; it does not apply an unimplemented or unproved transform.

items.title: Allocator policy beyond completed32/Q/R
items.current: Recordings32, epoch growth2MiB, available allocator slots8, per-kind idle packs8, combined idle budget64MiB. Q quiescent reset and R idle-first selection already exist.32/64 comparison is historical work, not a new module.
items.proposed: Change exactly one policy bound in one patch only after existing churn/idle/retained-byte counters identify its cause. Preserve the state machine and avoid a product setting or a second implementation lane.
stateTable: R existing idle-first selection; same accounting
Existing cleanup and error contract, no speculative recycle
counterexamples: Higher recording bound improves one microcase but grows transient command memory
A low available-pool count trades reuse for repeated allocation
Budget bytes are not physical APFS/RAM reclaim
Resetting an ended but unsubmitted recording violates native command ownership
items.missing: No new alternative value is supported by a distinct observed churn or memory-pressure cause. An arbitrary tuning constant is not a completed optimization.
items.nextEvidence: Read existing per-epoch reset/allocation/reuse and retained-byte observations on current R; choose one named workload and one value only if those observations explain it.
verification: Matched throughput plus peak retained memory for the one value
After native allocator retirement and only then pool reuse

items.title: General render-pass boundary removal beyond11a
items.current: 11a is a separate prepared upstream Typed buffer discard module. M4 render end currently sets fallback store actions, ends encoding, merges/satisfies dependencies, performs unsupported resolves, ends visibility work, then flushes timestamp samples in order.
items.proposed: Eliminate one repeated internal split only after identifying its command and proving all attachment/subresource/load-store, resource alias, sampling, query and dependency effects. Keep unknown boundaries unchanged.
stateTable: Same attachments, pure redundant state change
Candidate only if no intervening observer or encoder restriction
Keep helper ownership and original observation order
counterexamples: Same framebuffer pointer but different subresource or alias backing
No next draw after a split still requires final attachment content and queries
Moving timestamp flush before resolve/visibility changes query result meaning
Merging a pass across an upload can expose stale vertex/index data
items.missing: No specific BAR redundant split with all observers accounted for is identified.11a reducing the upstream split cause is an untested hypothesis, so rerank afterward instead of adding general merging now.
items.nextEvidence: Use an existing pass trace to name boundary command, exact before/after attachments, backing lifetimes, load/store actions and intervening observers. Inspect after11a activation.
verification: Existing suspend/resolve/visibility/alias native fixtures with the exact boundary
M3 unchanged path plus M4 relevant behavior

items.title: Intermediate MSAA resolve deferral
items.current: Existing internal private backing with storeOverride and resolve but without combined StoreResolve already selects Store; the final native pass resolves. Memoryless, format capability and depth/stencil swizzle determine different actions. AA Off is not proof of single-sample offscreen attachments.
items.proposed: Pre-classify one proven internal multisample split and its final consumer before native encoder creation. Keep all samples in a surviving private backing and resolve at its required observation/final boundary. No blanket Store-only override.
stateTable: Dirty samples; preserve backing and final resolve owner
Internal split with no observer and private stable backing
Final end, including no further draw
Exactly one required final resolve; no lost obligation
counterexamples: Omitting intermediate resolve then never starting another encoder loses final output
Memoryless backing cannot survive a plain Store/Load policy
Resolve target sampled between fragments requires intermediate value
Depth-only versus stencil-swizzled views cannot share guessed store rules
An extra final encoder may cost more than a deferred resolve saves
items.missing: No observed repeated eligible offscreen MSAA split with complete consumer/backing lifetime is identified; current narrow no-combined optimization already exists.
items.nextEvidence: Identify exact sample count, actual override backing storageMode, resolve format capability and final/intermediate observers for one current BAR split; align with11b.

items.title: Redundant dependency edge beyond completed E3
source: semantic signals, completion and allocator lifetime
items.current: Existing stage-pair source/visibility masks are grouped only for identical source requirements. satisfy follows actual emission. Prepared prefixes carry consumed destination obligations through incoming entry/outgoing exit. E3 compute coverage is a completed experimental/Combined candidate, not active in frozen R unless explicitly composed. R DependencyScopes has no satisfyAlreadyEmitted.
items.proposed: Remove one named redundant edge only when a previously issued edge provides equivalent ordering and memory visibility for every affected destination, with no intervening producer/incarnation change. Preserve semantic timeline/event signals and native retirement.
stateTable: Equivalent later request, no new producer
Cleanup and waiting threads still reach terminal condition
Completion proof mandatory regardless of CPU worker idle time
counterexamples: Same source stages but different destination stages
Execution ordering without required memory visibility
A new producer after the supposed covering barrier
Address reuse after a CPU callback but before GPU retirement
Removing a semantic signal because its consumer was not observed in one sample
items.missing: No exact remaining redundant edge, alternate issued coverage and critical-path interval have been established. Suppressing waits by category would violate the current correctness model.
items.nextEvidence: Name one edge tuple (queue/epoch, producer, consumer, stage scopes, visibility, resource incarnation, host/query/signal consumers) from existing dependency evidence; close every state transition before code.
verification: Existing queue-barrier-reuse, counter-completion and timeline fixtures
Compare emitted edge coverage and actual native output; source proofs alone are insufficient
